significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish that an internal trigger feature has a measurable "generalization surface" whose sharpness, semantic breadth, and dimensionality distinguish string from concept triggers and predict mitigation success; this is a form-(iii) predictive coupling, not merely feature existence. It establishes both a phenomenon—graded activation under trigger perturbations—and a moderately strong mechanism—the learned trigger feature and its geometry explain activation and constrain expected responses to unseen variants and the choice between ablation and retraining; this bears directly on the persistent-backdoor problem demonstrated by Hubinger et al.'s Sleeper Agents (2024). Verified false would distinguishably rule out smooth trigger geometry or its proposed coupling to backdoor type and mitigation for the asserted classes, although failure of synthesis alone would not rule out every internal-feature account. Topic substitution fails: generic mechanistic LLM-safety importance would not earn this score; the above-median value specifically comes from the quoted geometry-to-type-to-mitigation relation.

reach.justification: The claim hands auditors two named handles: "human-readable approximate triggers" and a "generalization-surface geometry (sharpness, semantic breadth, dimensionality)" fingerprint that routes mitigation. These are ex ante in the stated "open-weight supply-chain vetting" and "pre-deployment red-team" settings, providing time to seed targeted tests, canaries, or retraining before shipment rather than merely explaining an observed incident. Although quantities require re-extraction, the substantive conclusion predicts that newly extracted narrow surfaces indicate string triggers and favor targeted ablation, whereas broad semantic surfaces indicate concept triggers and favor retraining; its asserted scope spans several trigger classes and makes white-box auditors, red teams, and deployers downstream users, but it does not extend to closed APIs or guarantee transfer to naturally arising backdoors. Topic substitution fails: broad LLM-safety auditing alone would not justify this reach; it depends specifically on the quoted trigger-recovery and mitigation-routing handles.
